title: 9. Relationship Between CAG and Public Accounts Committee (PAC)

blocks.content: The CAG acts as a friend, philosopher, and guide to the Public Accounts Committee.

rows: 22 Members (15 from Lok Sabha, 7 from Rajya Sabha)
Audits public accounts and prepares technical audit reports
Examines CAG audit reports and evaluates executive financial conduct
Submits audit reports to the President / Governor
Submits findings and recommendations to Parliament

items: CAG submits reports to the President (or State Governor), who causes them to be laid before Parliament; CAG does not submit reports directly to the PAC.
The Chairman of the PAC is appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha and, by convention established in 1967, is selected from the Opposition.
PAC recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding on the government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) acts as a friend, philosopher, and guide to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).
CAG submits three audit reports to the President—on Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, and Public Undertakings—which are subsequently laid before Parliament.
The PAC scrutinizes the CAG's audit reports to ensure that public funds are spent in accordance with parliamentary sanctions and legal provisions.
The CAG attends the meetings of the PAC and assists the committee by explaining complex financial and auditing nuances.
While the CAG conducts technical financial auditing, the PAC provides parliamentary political oversight over executive expenditures.
